subject: ophthalmology
title: Diseases of the orbit

steps.tx: **Proptosis** (exophthalmos over 21 mm or asymmetry over 2 mm on Hertel) demands direction, duration and vision: axial proptosis points intraconal (optic nerve glioma, haemangioma), eccentric displacement points extraconal (lacrimal tumours superotemporal, mucoceles from sinuses, metastases). Red flags are pain, diplopia, vision loss, pulsation, bruit and systemic features. Workup pairs contrast CT or MRI (muscles, apex, sinuses, bone) with thyroid function, blood counts and biopsy of accessible lesions; cavernous haemangioma is the commonest benign adult orbital tumour.
steps.say: Measure it, watch which way it pushes, scan the apex. Axial means inside the muscle cone.

vis.alt: Comparison of axial proptosis from an intraconal orbital mass versus eccentric inferomedial globe displacement from a superotemporal extraconal lacrimal tumour or sinus mucocele.
vis.caption: Axial proptosis (intraconal mass) vs eccentric proptosis (extraconal orbital mass).

steps.tx: **Thyroid eye disease** (Graves orbitopathy) is the commonest proptosis cause overall: autoimmune fibroblast activation swells extraocular muscles (tendon sparing enlargement, inferior then medial rectus) and fat, giving lid retraction with lag, lid lag on downgaze (von Graefe), staring appearance, restrictive myopathy and compressive optic neuropathy at the apex. Activity scores (CAS) separate active (steroids, rituximab patterns, orbital radiotherapy) from burnt out fibrotic disease (strabismus then lid surgery, decompression for neuropathy or disfigurement). Smoking worsens and radioiodine can flare disease.
steps.say: Staring lids plus fat muscles sparing tendons: Graves orbit. Active disease gets steroids, quiet disease gets surgery.

vis.alt: Composite image of a patient with proptosis and lid retraction, next to a coronal CT scan showing enlarged inferior and medial rectus muscles, characteristic of Thyroid Eye Disease.
vis.caption: Thyroid eye disease: clinical signs and characteristic muscle enlargement on CT

steps.tx: **Orbital cellulitis** breaches the septum from ethmoid sinusitis (children through thin lamina), presenting with fever, painful proptosis, restricted painful eye movements, chemosis and vision threat, versus preseptal cellulitis where globe, movements and vision stay normal. Contrast CT grades Chandler spread (subperiosteal abscess displacing globe); IV broad antibiotics cover sinus flora urgently, with drainage for abscess, optic compromise or intracranial extension. Cavernous sinus thrombosis bilateralises chemosis with ophthalmoplegia, trigeminal signs and sepsis, needing MRI venography and anticoagulation debates in ICU care.
steps.say: Painful eye that cannot move with fever is post septal until scanned. Bilateral red frozen eyes mean cavernous sinus.

vis.alt: Sagittal and axial orbital views comparing preseptal cellulitis anterior to the orbital septum with postseptal orbital cellulitis and subperiosteal abscess from ethmoid sinusitis.
vis.caption: Preseptal cellulitis vs postseptal orbital cellulitis and subperiosteal abscess.

steps.tx: **Key point.** Vascular and malignant patterns complete the orbit: carotid cavernous fistula gives pulsatile proptosis with bruit and arterialised conjunctival vessels after trauma (direct) or spontaneously (indirect dural); retinoblastoma and rhabdomyosarcoma dominate childhood malignancy (rapid superonasal mass in rhabdomyosarcoma needing urgent biopsy and chemoradiation); adult metastases (breast, lung, prostate) and lymphoma (salmon patch, moulding without bony destruction) infiltrate insidiously. Optic nerve sheath meningioma shows tram track calcification with progressive vision loss.
steps.say: Pulsing eye with whoosh is fistula. Child with overnight ballooning upper lid mass: rhabdomyosarcoma.
